answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable stake for a long horizon before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify useful work. A juniper-style reputation score can weight those attestations, while slashing the stake when a claim is disproved. Creating a swarm then means tying up real capital in every identity and risking its loss; basalt-hard identity checks alone would not stop a well-funded attacker, but the stake makes Sybil influence costly rather than free.
